rows.figure: Beirut struck Sunday; signing test still a claim day
rows.read: Sunday's two developments. First, Israel struck Beirut's southern suburbs — the first strike since June — killing Hezbollah chief of staff Haytham Tabtabai (Hezbollah confirmed; 5 killed, 25 wounded per Lebanon health ministry). The IDF told northern-Israel residents to continue daily routines — no response anticipated as of now — but Hezbollah's political council is 'studying the matter of response.' Tehran insists the Lebanon front be part of any deal, so the strike lands on the negotiations. Second, the signing test became claim day: Trump's camp says the Iran deal is 'complete' while Tehran (Araqchi, via Reuters Sunday) says the Hormuz 7-day reopen offer is 'still on the table' but talks have stalled — and no Reuters/Bloomberg/CNBC/AP story of a signed deal exists as of 4pm CT. Aggregator 'markets celebrate' content is held, not used (its futures numbers don't survive arithmetic against Friday's verified settles). Saturday's ledger stands: IRGC declared Hormuz 'closed' vs Cooper's 'controlled by the United States' rebuttal; 12 vessels attacked in the week ended Friday — the largest weekly UKMTO tally of the war, with a new RPG-from-small-boat attack type; the IRGC mine claim has a second wire (AFP) but still zero independent confirmation. Sunday's UKMTO ledger, as reported claims: a tugboat hit by two projectiles off UAE (one minor casualty, no attribution), an LNG tanker fired on off Yemen (skiff turned away), and the Saudi-led coalition intercepting 2 Houthi missiles toward Khamis Mushait plus a drone toward Riyadh. Crude's Sunday open ~5pm CT prices it first; the haven read arrives at Monday's open.
